subject: Acme Retail - sudden spike in inference 5xx and tail-latency: tcp handshake / NAT / DNS scatter
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme-retail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: support@acme-retail.com
Date: 2028-09-06T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden spike in 5xx / tail-latency for inference calls (request ids attached)

Hi Naomi / Ben,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx error rates and 200+ ms tail-latency on our Redwood-powered recommendation endpoint around 14:40 PDT yesterday. Impact is customer-visible — checkout latency spikes, and retries cause timeouts on our side. Sample request IDs: req-4f3a, req-4f3b, req-4f4c.

Attached are a brief log sample and a Grafana screenshot showing the spike. Our network team sees a lot of SYN retransmits and occasional TCP RSTs in the same time window, and DNS lookups for api.redwood-inference.com sometimes return a set of IPs that change between retries. We suspect a path/peering or NAT issue between our VPC and Redwood's egress.

We need immediate troubleshooting and a temporary mitigation — this is affecting two regions of our checkout flow. Can we get a call and a runbook? If this is a routing issue on Redwood's side, we will need an exec escalation.

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of Platform
Acme Retail

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-09-06T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden spike in 5xx / tail-latency for inference calls (initial triage)

Internal triage notes — initial findings below.

Observed:
- Correlation with increased SYN retransmits and RSTs in Acme's pcaps; many handshakes complete after 2–3 retransmits (tail-latency hit).
- DNS behavior: api.redwood-inference.com resolves to multiple A records that spread connections across 3 egress IPs. Acme's traces show different downstream peers depending on which IP is used.
- On our side, egress telemetry for the timestamps in Acme's logs shows intermittent elevated p95 latency from a subset of NAT IPs in us-west-2.

Hypothesis:
- Route asymmetry / peering flapping causing slightly different AS paths to different egress IPs. Some paths appear to be traversing a firewall/proxy cluster that is terminating long-lived connections prematurely (RST or aggressive timeout).
- DNS A-record rotation + client resolver behavior is scattering connections across those paths, exposing Acme to the worse path intermittently — this explains spike and variability.

Immediate mitigations to propose to customer:
1) Pin resolution to a single stable egress IP (hosts override) to force a single path while we debug.
2) Use our dedicated endpoint (dedicated IP) if Acme can switch temporarily — avoids shared NAT with other tenants.
3) We will coordinate with infra to rotate the problematic NAT cluster out of the rotation and hold it out for additional instrumentation.

Action items:
- Karthik: start BGP/peering checks for us-west-2 and check recent route changes/withdrawals.
- Marissa: prepare customer-facing mitigation steps and hosts override instruction.
- Ben / Naomi: propose a 30-min exec sync if root cause points to peering.

Soojin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acme-retail.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-06T15:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 5xx / tail-latency for inference calls (workaround steps)

Carlos — quick follow-up with a low-friction mitigation you can try immediately.

Option A — hosts override (fastest, no infra change):
- Edit /etc/hosts (or equivalent) on a small set of test app hosts and map api.redwood-inference.com -> 52.8.140.22 (we believe .22 is one of the stable egress IPs).
- Test 50–100 requests from a replica to see if tail-latency / 5xx drop.

Option B — dedicated endpoint:
- If you have traffic shaping available, route a small percentage of requests to the dedicated endpoint we can provision; this isolates you from the shared NAT pool.

I’ve attached step-by-step hosts override instructions. If you can run the hosts test and send results (and any tcpdumps) we’ll proceed.

Thanks — we’ll also keep the war-room open for live debugging.

Attachment: hosts-workaround-instructions.txt (text)

Ben Carter

Subject: Exec brief: Acme Retail customer-impacting latency and 5xx — proposed immediate actions

Vivek / Rishi — quick summary and ask for prioritization.

Summary:
- Impact: Acme (large retail account, checkout-critical) experienced p95/p99 tail-latency spikes and a transient increase in 5xx beginning 2028-09-06T14:40 PDT. Customer-visible, increased retries and failed checkouts reported.
- Triage: SRE (Soojin) observed correlation with a subset of egress NAT IPs in us-west-2; DNS rotation is distributing Acme's traffic across multiple egress paths. Network Eng (Karthik) investigating BGP/peering history.
- Hypothesis: Path asymmetry + firewall/proxy cluster on one path introducing premature connection termination.

Immediate proposed actions (needs priority & capacity):
1) Approve an emergency NAT-node rotation to remove the suspicious NAT cluster from rotation while we gather instrumentation (2–4 hours).
2) Grant authorization to provision a dedicated endpoint for Acme to provide isolation (temporary, can be rolled back).
3) Prepare a customer-facing post-mitigation note and offer a credit if SLA thresholds were breached during the incident window.

Customer ask: they are running the hosts workaround test now. If it validates, we can roll a more durable routing change.

Request: please confirm approval for actions (1) and (2) so we can execute immediately.

Marissa Cole
Head of Support, Redwood Inference

- Customer credit recommendation for account team to review.

Keep me in the loop on test results from the hosts override. If customer impact continues after mitigations, escalate to channel ops for a full peering review.

Rishi
